newsitem.title: UK: British farmers hand out free beef.
newsitem.headline: British farmers hand out free beef.

text.p: British farmers handed out free beefburgers and held barbecues in town centres across the country on Saturday in a bid to persuade people that beef is safe to eat.
Thousands of farmers, butchers and restaurants joined forces to provide giveaways at motorway service stations and cookery demonstrations in shopping centres to mark National Beef Day.

The events were organised by the National Farmers Union following fresh scientific evidence this week suggesting a link between mad cow disease and the fatal human brain condition Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).
Farmers said there had been huge demand for the free beef despite research that showed a new variant of CJD left traces very similar to those found in bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

"We had three people cooking the beefburgers as fast as they can, but we couldn't satisfy the demand. People were coming from all directions. I have never seen so many people queuing," said dairy farmer Mary James in the western city of Bristol.
"It has all been tremendously worthwhile, people are very supportive. We regard this as a thank you to them," James added.
Beef sales in Britain fell to just over 70 percent of normal when the BSE scare broke in March but have now recovered to about 85 percent.
The European Union said on Thursday it would maintain its seven-month ban on British beef and urged Britain to implement an eradication plan agreed in June.
The London government last month put a proposed cull of 147,000 cattle on hold after some experts said BSE would die out naturally early in the 21st century.
In some parts of Britain on Saturday, farmers brought prize cattle into town and one group sponsored a horse race.

"Many people seemed desperate to come up and tell us that they are still eating beef," said Jeremy Bailey, chairman of the Farmers Union branch in the Salisbury. "People are grabbing stickers to show their support. They have slogans like "I am eating British beef'."
